source.title: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization
source.authors: Bingjun Luo; Jialin Guo; Yue Yao; Xinpeng Ding

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports visual-style jailbreak results for VLMs, but neither tests the listed claims about safety fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant openings, safety-localized parameters, or deepening safety training, nor relies on those findings as a tool.
record.gate_note: The study measures harmful-completion attack success after applying visual style modifications to attack images. This is a related but different bypass mechanism from the compliant openings, suffixes, and decoding changes in V4. The results are recorded with versions ["none"]. It does not test benign or harmful fine-tuning of the safety-trained model, response-position KL, or weight localization.
record.test_reason: The study measures how much optimized visual-style edits to existing jailbreak images raise HarmBench-judged ASR on VLMs. It never fine-tunes the target models (V1, V2) or measures per-token KL (V3). It tests no prefills, suffixes or decoding changes (V4), does no weight localization (V5), and proposes no cause (V6) or deepening fix (V7). Image-style perturbation is an input-content attack, not an attack on the response opening. The shallow-alignment work is not cited or relied on. The rows compare the study's own attack-enhancement method with base attacks, so they belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors further claim that VLM safety depends on how an image is styled, not only on its content. They also say ASR gains are usually accompanied by higher Harmfulness Scores, and that most of the gain comes from the RL enhancement stage rather than probing. They describe the gains as near-universal, although GPT-4.1-mini on HIMRD decreased.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizes stylistic changes to adversarial images using an image-editing generator and GRPO; it does not fine-tune the safety-trained target model or measure response-token distributions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by target VLM, base attack, and benchmark. The study also distinguishes naive style probing from RL-based enhancement.

fits_no_version.finding: RL-optimized visual style edits to existing jailbreak images raise HarmBench ASR on Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-OV-1.5, GPT-4.1-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash by about 1–8 points. Gains vary by model, base attack and benchmark, and ASR falls in one case (GPT-4.1-mini HIMRD, 72.80%→71.77%). Naive best-style probing gives smaller gains (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visual-style modifications of attack images can amplify existing VLM jailbreaks, with model- and attack-dependent gains.

record.problems: The reported ASR results provide no uncertainty estimates. The paper does not report a capability-retention evaluation. Its category breakdown in Table 3 does not identify the target model in the presented table, so category-specific values are not extracted as model-level rows.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports category-level ASR and Harmfulness Score breakdowns for QR Attack, SI Attack, and HIMRD. Those results are not extracted because the presented table does not identify the target model, and the category-level layout does not support assigning them to a specific model. Harmfulness Score values are also not added as separate rows because the paper presents ASR as the main attack-success metric and does not compare HS as a competing measure.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning of the safety-trained model; no target-model fine-tuning is done.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes and decoding changes. Only image-style edits are tested.
Localization of safety in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or the training objective produces shallowness.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens, and its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: Relation 'discusses' is kept only because the paper discusses safety-alignment jailbreaks in general; it does not engage the shallow-alignment claim or its originals. All rows measure the study's own method against base attacks. No uncertainty is reported, and the judge is HarmBench only.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, suffixes, and decoding changes; the paper instead tests visual-style image modifications.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or a training objective produces safety shallowness.
Training to spread safety beyond initial tokens and its robustness.

relation.reason: It discusses safety-alignment vulnerabilities generally, without testing the specified shallow-alignment mechanisms or using them as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study optimizes visual styles by training an image-editing generator and evaluates target VLM jailbreak ASR. It neither tests nor uses V1–V7.

source_check.notes: All sampled numbers match their table cells. These rows compare the study's own attack method and ablations; they fit no claim version and should not be treated as phenomenon evidence.
